chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-qual-03.title: Triangle area
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-qual-03.body:
The graph of $y=20-|x|$ is a triangle with base $40$ and height $20$, of area $\frac12\cdot40\cdot20=400$.

**Answer: 400**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-qual-06.title: Substitution
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-qual-06.body:
With $u=x^3-3x$, $du=3(x^2-1)dx$, and the limits become $u=0$ to $u=2$. (Here $u^{4/3}=(\sqrt[3]{u})^4$ is the real power; $u$ is negative on part of the range.) The integral is $\frac13\left[\frac{3}{7}u^{7/3}\right]_0^2=\frac17\,2^{7/3}$.

**Answer: $\frac{2^{7/3}}{7}$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-qual-07.title: Divide by $x^2$
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-qual-07.body:
Dividing numerator and denominator by $x^2$: $\frac{2x-1/x^2}{x^2+1/x}$. The numerator is the derivative of the denominator, so the integral is $\left[\ln\!\left(x^2+\frac1x\right)\right]_1^2=\ln\frac92-\ln2=\ln\frac94$.

**Answer: $\ln\frac94$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-qual-08.title: Fractional part
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-qual-08.body:
On each interval $[k,k+1]$ the integrand $\{x\}$ has integral $\frac12$. There are $2024$ intervals, so the integral is $1012$.

**Answer: 1012**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-qual-09.title: King's rule
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-qual-09.body:
Replace $x$ by $\pi-x$: $\cos(\pi-x)=-\cos x$, so $I=\int_0^\pi\frac{e^{-\cos x}}{e^{\cos x}+e^{-\cos x}}dx$. Adding, $2I=\int_0^\pi1\,dx=\pi$, so $I=\frac\pi2$.

**Answer: $\frac\pi2$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-qual-11.title: Substitute $u=\ln x$
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-qual-11.body:
With $u=\ln x$, $x=e^u$, $dx=e^udu$ and $x^{\ln x-1}=e^{u(u-1)}$: the integrand becomes $e^{u^2-u}\cdot u\cdot e^u=ue^{u^2}$. So the integral is $\int_0^1ue^{u^2}du=\frac{e-1}2$.

**Answer: $\frac{e-1}2$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-qual-12.title: Substitute and integrate by parts
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-qual-12.body:
With $x=e^u$: $I=\int_{-\infty}^\pi e^u\sin u\,du$. Since $\frac d{du}\left[\frac{e^u(\sin u-\cos u)}2\right]=e^u\sin u$,
$$I=\left[\frac{e^u(\sin u-\cos u)}2\right]_{-\infty}^{\pi}=\frac{e^\pi\,(0+1)}2=\frac{e^\pi}2.$$

**Answer: $\frac{e^\pi}2$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-qual-13.title: Find an antiderivative
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-qual-13.body:
$\frac d{dx}\left[\frac x{1+\ln x}\right]=\frac{(1+\ln x)-1}{(1+\ln x)^2}=\frac{\ln x}{(1+\ln x)^2}$. So the integral is $\frac e2-\frac11=\frac e2-1$.

**Answer: $\frac e2-1$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-qual-14.title: Floor takes values $0$ and $-1$
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-qual-14.body:
On $\left[\frac1{k+1},\frac1k\right]$ the angle $\frac\pi x$ ranges over $[k\pi,(k+1)\pi]$. There $\sin$ is $\le0$ when $k$ is odd (floor $=-1$ except at endpoints) and $\ge0$ when $k$ is even (floor $=0$, except where $\sin=1$, a null set). Hence
$$\int_0^1=-\sum_{k\text{ odd}}\left(\frac1k-\frac1{k+1}\right)=-\left(1-\frac12+\frac13-\cdots\right)=-\ln2.$$

**Answer: $-\ln2$**
